slides.title: The Story
slides.subtitle: Before we read, we need to understand the 'mood' of our novel. Let's find out what kind of story this is!

slides.title: HOW TO: Identify Genre
slides.content: Keyword Hunt: Scan 'About the Author' (p.144) Para 2 & 3 for descriptors. Look for specific literary traditions mentioned in the text.

slides.title: TASK 1 | Genre Check
slides.rationale: Decide if this is horror, sci-fi, or comedy. (Scan 'About the Author' p.144)
slides.content:
Classic horror storyComedy
BiographyEarly science fiction
History bookTravel writing

slides.title: ANSWER 1
slides.answer: Classic horror story & Early science fiction
slides.evidence: [Para 3] 'often called the first science fiction novel... follows the Gothic tradition.'
slides.explanation: Mary Shelley combined old scary 'Gothic' elements with new scientific ideas to create something completely new.

slides.title: HOW TO: Scan for Bio
slides.content: Scan Facts: Don't read every word! Find the names and years first. Where was Mary born? Where was she in 1816?

slides.title: TASK 2 | The Idea
slides.content:

Scan Paras 1-2 for when, where and how Mary got the idea.

slides.title: ANSWER 2
slides.answer: WHEN: Summer 1816 | WHERE: Near Geneva | HOW: A powerful vision
slides.evidence: [Para 2] 'stormy night in the summer of 1816... staying with... Lord Byron near Geneva... had a powerful vision'
slides.explanation: Mary was only 19 when she had the vision during a ghost story competition with friends.

slides.title: New Words
slides.subtitle: Let's master 5 tricky words so the story is easy to understand. Ready?

slides.context_sentence: Victor built a 150-meter metal mast above his laboratory to catch the lightning.
Victor looked at the creature's thin, yellow skin and saw an awful smile on its face.
Victor was irresponsible because he forgot about his family and letters for two years.
Victor's work was obsessive; he worked every day and night without a single holiday.
Instead of being careful, Victor's reckless use of electricity caused a huge disaster.

slides.title: The Big Secret
slides.subtitle: We are now going to read about Victor and his creation of Frankenstein! As you read, take a note of how the story unfolds and get ready to do exercise Task 5 in your book.

slides.title: Reading Time
slides.content:
READ for pleasure! Pages 144-147.
05:00

slides.title: TASK 3 | The Journey
right_items: A. He worked hard on his machine.
B. He was given his own laboratory.
C. He woke up and saw the creature.
D. He learned about death in hospitals.
F. The electricity brought the creature to life.
slides.notes: Have students discuss the order in pairs before you click to reveal.

slides.title: TASK 3 | Correct Order
right_items: D. He learned about death in hospitals.
B. He was given his own laboratory.
A. He worked hard on his machine.
F. The electricity brought the creature to life.
C. He woke up and saw the creature.
slides.notes: Notice how Victor's ambition led him from education to isolation.

slides.title: ANSWER 3
slides.evidence: [Para 1] Met Waldman → [Para 5] Learned about death → [Para 8] Given laboratory → [Para 4] Two years work → [Para 17] Body came alive → [Para 20] Woke to see creature.
slides.explanation: Victor's journey: First Waldman inspired him, then he studied death, got a lab, worked obsessively, succeeded with electricity, and finally faced his creation in fear.

slides.title: The Lessons
slides.subtitle: Now we know the plot, let's look closer at Victor's big mistakes.

slides.title: STRATEGY: Probing the Protagonist
slides.content:
WHAT: Analyzing 'Character Flaws' (Hubris).
WHY: To understand how Victor’s internal choices drive the external tragedy.
HOW: Scan the text for descriptors of Victor’s work habits and decisions (Page 147).

slides.title: TASK 8 | Victor's Flaws
slides.rationale: Which THREE words describe Victor's bad character? (Page 147)
slides.content:
AmbitiousObsessive
RecklessBrave
IrresponsibleSelfish

slides.title: ANSWER 8
slides.evidence: [Page 147] 'Victor's flawed character leads him to take the disastrous path...' The text identifies these three specific character flaws.
slides.explanation: Victor was obsessive (worked without holidays), irresponsible (ignored his family), and reckless (used dangerous electricity without thinking).

slides.title: STRATEGY: Identifying Themes
slides.content:
WHAT: Discovering the 'Moral of the Story'.
WHY: To connect the character's actions to universal warnings.
HOW: Look for paragraphs where the author addresses the reader directly (Page 147).

slides.title: TASK 9 | Big Ideas
slides.rationale: Which TWO themes does Mary Shelley want us to think about? (Page 147)
slides.content:
Love conquers allDangerous Knowledge
MoralityTechnology is evil

slides.title: ANSWER 9
slides.evidence: [Page 147] 'dangerous and forbidden knowledge' and 'morals and distinguishing right from wrong'
slides.explanation: Shelley warns us: some knowledge is dangerous, and we must always ask 'is this right?' before we act.

slides.title: The Verdict
slides.subtitle: Victor made his choice, then he ran away in fear. Now it's your turn to judge his actions.

slides.title: DEBATE | Who is the Monster?
slides.content:
Who is more to blame for the tragedy?
VICTOR
He played God but was irresponsible and reckless.		THE CREATURE
He is 2.5 meters tall, awful to look at, and scary.
03:00
slides.notes: Encourage students to use the vocabulary from Phase 2 (reckless, obsessive, irresponsible) in their arguments.
